feedback.worked_solution:
Let's remind ourselves of the special trigonometric ratios, as given by the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13942110/assets/dbf36192ac332dc49ed75278838e989a37ac7d888311be1b8b059a7b59667aa6.png)

From the unit circle, we see that the angle $\frac{7\pi }{6}$ corresponds to the point $(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},-\frac{1}{2}).$

Since the sine of the angle corresponds to the $y$-coordinate, we have $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})=-\frac{1}{2}.$

Therefore, using the fact that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})}=\frac{1}{(-\frac{1}{2})}=-2.
$$

Finally, evaluating $v(t)$ at $t=\frac{7\pi }{6}$ we have

$$
2{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})=2{(-2)}^{2}=8.
$$
